knowledge:
- key_parameters: subject=The second argument, which can be genomic ranges (GenomicRanges, RangedSummarizedExperiment) or sequences (DNAStringSet, DNAString, character vector) ;; genome=Required if subject is genomic ranges; can be a BSgenome object, DNAStringSet, or FaFile ;; bg=Background nucleotide frequencies; can be "even", "genome", or a named numeric vector ;; out=Output type; "matches" (default, returns boolean matrix), "scores" (returns boolean matrix, high scores, and match counts), or "positions" (returns GenomicRangesList or IRangesList)
- alternatives: matchPWM in Biostrings and searchSeq in TFBSTools are alternatives, but motifmatchr is preferred when matching many different sequences/ranges against many different motifs
- when_to_use: Use when scanning a large set of genomic ranges (such as ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq peaks) or sequences against a large database of motifs (such as JASPAR) to find matches, scores, or exact match positions
- pitfalls: Default background frequencies are calculated from input sequences, which may not be appropriate for short sequences (use bg = "even" or bg = "genome" instead) ;; Using bg = "genome" requires specifying a genome ;; If background frequencies passed to matchMotifs do not match those in the input PWM, the PWM is adjusted, changing the calculated scores; ensure background frequencies match the bg slot of the PWMatrix object to avoid this ;; If the subject is a sequence object (character vector, DNAStringSet, DNAString) and no ranges argument is provided, out = "positions" returns relative positions (IRangesList) instead of genomic coordinates (GenomicRangesList)

workflows.name: motif_matching_genomic_ranges
workflows.intent: Find motif matches, scores, and genomic positions within a set of genomic ranges (peaks).
input: example_motifs (PWMatrixList or PFMatrixList containing motif matrices)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the motifmatchr, GenomicRanges, SummarizedExperiment, and BSgenome libraries ;; 2. Load example motifs and define genomic ranges (peaks) ;; 3. Find motif matches using matchMotifs with default settings ;; 4. Extract the boolean matches matrix using motifMatches ;; 5. Find motif matches and extract scores and counts using out = "scores" ;; 6. Find exact genomic positions of motif matches using out = "positions"
workflows.code:
library(motifmatchr)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(BSgenome)

data(example_motifs, package = "motifmatchr") 

peaks <- GRanges(seqnames = c("chr1","chr2","chr2"),
                 ranges = IRanges(start = c(76585873,42772928,100183786),
                                  width = 500))

motif_ix <- matchMotifs(example_motifs, peaks, genome = "hg19") 
motifMatches(motif_ix)

motif_ix_scores <- matchMotifs(example_motifs, peaks, 
                                genome = "hg19", out = "scores")
head(motifMatches(motif_ix_scores))
head(motifScores(motif_ix_scores))
head(motifCounts(motif_ix_scores))

motif_pos <- matchMotifs(example_motifs, peaks, genome = "hg19", 
                          out = "positions") 
print(motif_pos)

workflows.name: motif_matching_sequences
workflows.intent: Find motif matches directly within biological sequences (DNAStringSet or character vectors).
input: example_motifs (PWMatrixList or PFMatrixList containing motif matrices)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the Biostrings and genome libraries ;; 2. Extract sequences from the genome using genomic ranges ;; 3. Find motif matches using a DNAStringSet input ;; 4. Convert sequences to a character vector and find motif matches
workflows.code:
library(Biostrings)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19)

example_DNAStringSet <- getSeq(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19, peaks)

motif_ix_DNAStringSet <- matchMotifs(example_motifs, example_DNAStringSet) 

example_character <- as.character(example_DNAStringSet)

motif_ix_character <- matchMotifs(example_motifs, example_character)
